title: Krónos: the restoration, the temple, and the world it opens

body:
# Krónos: the restoration, the temple, and the world it opens
The domain you're reading about exists because someone refused to let **Krónos** stay *kronos*.

Krónos is the hinge between the primordial gods and the Olympian order. His myth is the myth of generational succession — the son who overthrows the father and is in turn overthrown. Ouranos hated the children Gaia bore him and hid them inside her.  Gaia fashioned a great stone sickle and persuaded her sons to avenge her.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Krónos
- **ASCII form:** kronos
- **Meaning:** "Youngest Titan, personification of time, who castrated and deposed his father Uranus before being overthrown by his son Zeus"
- **Domain of influence:** Time, Harvest, Titans
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Classification:** Tier 2
- **Original script:** Κρόνος
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 132 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **Κρόνος**. On the evidence, it means "Youngest Titan, personification of time, who castrated and deposed his father Uranus before being overthrown by his son Zeus".

Strip **Krónos** to *kronos* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **o → ó** — Acute stress on the first omicron: the stress position the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Krónos** lives at [/sites/kronos/](/sites/kronos/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/kronos/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/kronos/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/kronos/patterns/).

The restoration preserves one decisive feature the ASCII form drops — a single, honest mark — which places it in Tier-2: exact, and exactly labeled.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Krónos** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Timekeeping & Calendar Systems** — Time personified; chronograph, chronology, chronic — his name keeps the hours.
- **Agriculture, Food & Harvest** — The sickle-bearing Titan of the harvest.
- **Ancestry & Heritage Services** — Father of six Olympians; the ruling dynasty's patriarch and cautionary progenitor.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Greek tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), and [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
## The File Continues

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/kronos/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.
